# Istrek 0.9.5
`istrekctl` remembers its sign-in, agent and reader credentials can be created on the web, the Mac app's first run always offers a way to run your own server, and a hosted server gains terms and a privacy notice.
Nothing changes in the API. Clients of 0.6.0 and later are served.
## New
- **`istrekctl` reads the file `istrekctl login` saves.** After you sign in, every command uses that connection by itself, with no `ISTREK_CONNECTION` to export. The file is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/istrek/connection.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, otherwise `~/.config/istrek/connection.json`. `ISTREK_CONNECTION`, and `ISTREK_URL` with `ISTREK_TOKEN`, still come first when they are set. `istrekctl version` finds the file the same way. - **Signing in again replaces the file safely.** A second `istrekctl login` writes the new credential to a private file beside the old one and only then puts it in its place, so a sign-in that fails or is denied leaves your old connection as it was. - **Agent and reader credentials on the web.** The devices page of your account has a **Create a credential** form: give it a name, choose Agent or Reader, and the next page shows the token once, with the server, API and MCP addresses to use it with and a connection file for `istrekctl`. These credentials are listed and revoked like any other. Owner and importer credentials are not offered there. A read-only account cannot create one until a plan is paid; revoking still works. - **Terms and privacy pages on Istrek Cloud.** A hosted server serves `/terms` and `/privacy`, linked from the foot of the public pages and named on the sign-in page, the pricing card and the billing page. The privacy notice describes only what the server has switched on (sign-in protection, single sign-on, payments, analytics). On a self-hosted server both addresses answer 404.
## Changed
- **Clearer `istrekctl login` failures.** The messages speak of the terminal and the browser, not the Mac app, and the common failures have their own exit codes: 64 for an address that is not `https://` (or `http://` on localhost), 77 when the request is denied or the code expires, 75 when the server cannot be reached or is busy. The help lists exit code 76 (this `istrekctl` and the server do not work together) and says where the connection comes from. - **The default server is called Istrek Cloud.** `istrekctl login` without an address signs in to Istrek Cloud at `https://istrek.souris.cloud` and says so on its first line. - **Download links follow `ISTREK_UPDATE_URL`.** With it set, the landing page, the account overview and an empty devices page link to **Get the Mac app and istrekctl** at that address. Without it they say that the Mac app and `istrekctl` are not released yet, and that the account pages, the API and the MCP endpoint work now. - **The devices page names your own server.** An empty devices page on a self-hosted server tells you to choose My own server with this server's address, or to run `istrekctl login` with it, and never points you at Istrek Cloud. - **The Mac app's first run.** The sheet offers four cards: Istrek Cloud, My own server, Run your own server and Look around first. **Run your own server** is always there, slightly dimmed until you point at it or select it, so Istrek Cloud stays the first choice. Its pane says the server is free to run on a Linux machine, links the self-hosting guide and the downloads, and **Connect to your server** takes you to My own server. The Istrek Cloud pane has no default button any more: pressing Return on an untouched sheet signs in nowhere. - **Help in the Mac app** explains the trial, the subscription and the read-only account only when the connected server bills, and no longer states prices; the account page shows them. - **Updates in the Mac app.** The built-in updater starts only in a build signed by its developer. A build signed on your own Mac does not run it, and **Check for Updates…** is shown only where it works. - **No VAT on Istrek Cloud.** The seller is not a VAT payer, so no VAT is added to the prices, for consumers and businesses alike, and the amounts shown are final. The pages and e-mails say so, and the payment page and every invoice carry "Not a VAT payer (neplátce DPH)." You can still give a VAT ID; it is printed on your invoices and changes nothing in the amount. - **Accepting the terms at payment.** On Istrek Cloud, the payment page has a box you tick to accept the terms and to ask for the paid plan to start at once. It also says that a consumer who withdraws within 14 days is refunded the payment minus the days used. - **Pricing on the landing page.** The hosted card is called Istrek Cloud. While payments are off, the landing page promises no trial and no read-only state. - **The self-hosting guide** signs in with `istrekctl login https://time.example.com` and checks the connection with `istrekctl me`. It says that `ISTREK_HOSTED` and `ISTREK_BILLING` are the switches of Istrek Cloud and not meant for a server you run, and that the analytics and IndexNow keys serve only its landing page. - **Security updates.** The server's dependencies were updated for security fixes, among them its web server (Bandit) and its HTTP client. - **The licence** says that the Mac app asks GitHub (`raw.githubusercontent.com`) whether an update is available, and that starting it with `ISTREK_DISABLE_UPDATES=1` turns that off.
## Removed
- The landing page's film and its poster, which no page showed, are no longer shipped or served.
## Before you update
- No migration and no new required setting. 0.6.0 and later clients are served. - If you run `istrekctl` with neither `ISTREK_CONNECTION` nor `ISTREK_TOKEN` set and a connection file sits at the default path, commands now use it instead of stopping with a missing-credential error. - If you link to the film or its poster from anywhere, those links now answer 404.
## Known limits
- The Mac app (`Istrek-VERSION.dmg`) and `istrekctl-VERSION.zip` are not published yet. - Only the amd64 build of the server is published. - Google's tag cannot be unloaded: when a visitor withdraws consent, Google Analytics stops from the next page on. Clarity stops at once. - Istrek has not been audited or penetration-tested by an outside party.
